headline_marked: 18,000 police to be deployed as [[DMP secures Dhaka for Awami League anniversary]]
headline: 18,000 police to be deployed as DMP secures Dhaka for Awami League anniversary
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police will set up over 200 checkpoints and deploy specialized units to prevent clashes and maintain order during the party's founding anniversary.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is deploying 18,000 officers and establishing more than 200 special checkpoints across the capital on Tuesday to secure the Awami League's founding anniversary.

The security measures come amid warnings of potential disorder and clashes between Awami League supporters and other groups, including the National Citizen Party (NCP) and the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.
Police Headquarters has instructed field-level units nationwide to remain vigilant, as activists of the banned party may attempt to hoist flags and hold public processions.
Specialized units, including the Detective Branch (DB) and Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit, will be active throughout the day to ensure public safety.
The Special Branch (SB) and Internal Affairs Division (IAD) will conduct plain-clothes intelligence operations to prevent potential sabotage or conspiracies.
Fifteen quick response teams and reserve forces at four major control rooms will be on standby to respond immediately to any emergencies.
The Awami League's activities remain banned following the departure of Sheikh Hasina on August 5, 2024, and subsequent trials over allegations of crimes against humanity.
Despite the ban, police continue to report sporadic processions and occasional arrests linked to the party's activities across the country.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman: [[2,000+ Bangladeshis to be freed]] in Malaysia
headline: PM Tarique Rahman: 2,000+ Bangladeshis to be freed in Malaysia
summary: The Prime Minister promised productive discussions with the Malaysian government to secure the release of detained citizens during a meeting with expats in Kuala Lumpur.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that the government will engage in productive discussions with the Malaysian government to free more than 2,000 Bangladeshis currently detained there.

Speaking at an exchange meeting with expatriate Bangladeshis in Kuala Lumpur on Sunday, the PM emphasized that the government is working to secure the best possible facilities for expats within the legal framework.

To reduce the migration of unskilled workers, the PM stated that technical institutions in Bangladesh are being made more effective. He also announced that basic Arabic will be mandatory for those heading to the Middle East within the next year.
The PM further revealed plans to make five languages, including English, and sports mandatory in school syllabuses for future generations to ensure they are are better equipped for the global market.
Regarding domestic development, the PM noted that 1,000 kilometers of canal excavation has been completed, though work will pause next month due to the monsoon season.

He urged the public to remain patient and hardworking, stating that Bangladesh has immense potential and that he does not wish to seek revenge for what happened to his family, focusing instead on duty and national progress.
caption:
Over 2,000 Bangladeshis are detained in Malaysia. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has promised their release.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that the government will engage in productive discussions with the Malaysian government to free more than 2,000 Bangladeshis currently detained there.

Speaking at an exchange meeting with expatriate Bangladeshis in Kuala Lumpur on Sunday, the PM emphasized that the government is working to secure the best possible facilities for expats within the legal framework.

To reduce the migration of unskilled workers, the PM stated that technical institutions in Bangladesh are being made more effective. He also announced that basic Arabic will be mandatory for those heading to the Middle East within the next year.

The PM further revealed plans to make five languages, including English, and sports mandatory in school syllabuses for future generations to ensure they are are better equipped for the global market.

Regarding domestic development, the PM noted that 1,000 kilometers of canal excavation has been completed, though work will pause next month due to the monsoon season.

He urged the public to remain patient and hardworking, stating that Bangladesh has immense potential and that he does not wish to seek revenge for what happened to his family, focusing instead on duty and national progress.
